title: Are the diagnostics reported alongside a population adjustment classifiers of its error?
question: Every population adjustment arrives with a panel of numbers beside it: effective sample size, the same figure as a percentage, the largest weight, standardized differences before and after adjustment, a distance between populations. A committee reads them as evidence about whether to believe the estimate. Scored as classifiers of realized error, with discrimination and calibration, against known truth and under a declared distribution of analyses, what are they worth?
design: An anchored indirect comparison with a continuous outcome and an identity link, chosen so that realized error decomposes exactly into arm imbalance, transport error and outcome noise, and a covariate diagnostic can be scored against the only component it could possibly know about. 128 cells crossing an omitted effect modifier, a cross-moment modifier no baseline table could reveal, overlap, source size, how correlated the omitted modifier is with the adjustment set, and a target dispersion ratio that destroys effective sample size while adding no bias at all. 4000 replicates per cell, three estimators.
estimand: Transported A versus C mean difference in the target superpopulation; the anchored A versus B contrast as a secondary reference
